approach: Add `PlanEntry::fix` (serde-skipped when false) and change the one sort in `Plan::build_with` (plan.rs:783) from `(e.rung, age)` to `(!e.fix, e.rung, age)`. That sort sees only the dependency-free ready items of the best effective priority (plan.rs:767-782), so the flag cannot beat priority or dependencies. `build_capped` and `build_improving` call `build_with`, so `athena plan` and `athena drain` get the rule from that one key. The flag comes from what the records link, by one new function, `hestia::fix_requests_of(records)`. It returns (a) the open steward-channel requests (`steward::improvement_requests`) unless the request's own text names only website or study content paths (new `reading::is_website_request`), (b) Hestia's waiting root-cause requests (the keys of `improvement_of(..).cause_jobs`) and (c) waiting requests holding a `Gate under review: NAME.` line. `drain.rs` computes the set once per `queue()` and once per `plan_entry()` and sets `entry.fix` in `entry_of`. The order text is updated where it would otherwise be false: the plan.rs and drain.rs docs, the `athena drain --help` Order text, README.md and roles-and-ladder.md. D181 and CHANGELOG.md record the rule and its limits. Revision, by finding. 5: the steward-channel rule replaces the work-item lookup (decision 2); the content guard reads the request text. 6: the website paths are named and tested (decision 3). 7: the cap-slot consequence goes in the CHANGELOG entry and the help text as well as D181 (decision 5). 1 to 4: the four files outside the listed deliverables stay, each with its reason (decision 6).

decisions.choice: Put the fix flag first in the `build_with` sort key, `(!e.fix, e.rung, age)`, after the best-effective-priority filter.
decisions.reason: Root cause of the starvation: inside a tier the order is rung then age (plan.rs:783), and nothing ranks a request that fixes Athena above feature work. The ready set is already cut to dependency-free items (plan.rs:767-775) of the best effective priority (plan.rs:780-781), so priority, the urgent and high caps and dependencies cannot be overridden. `priority_violations` compares priority only (plan.rs:633), so it stays correct. Every caller of `build_with` gets the rule.

rejected.option: Raise fix requests one priority tier in memory, as `build_improving` does for repeated causes (plan.rs:907-919).
rejected.why: It would beat person-set urgent and high work and use the capped urgent and high slots. 'Changing priority levels, caps' is out of scope.

rejected.option: Re-prioritise individual items, or rely on the guaranteed turn (IMPROVEMENT_GAP = 2, plan.rs:466).
rejected.why: The turn moves one request in three; the comment at plan.rs:877 records 5 of 32 steward requests running. The brief asks for the sort key to change.

decisions.choice: Finding 5: classify by channel and typed links in `hestia::fix_requests_of`. An open steward-channel request (`steward::improvement_requests`, steward.rs:376-390) is a fix unless `reading::is_website_request` holds for its own text. Hestia's waiting root-cause requests (keys of `improvement_of(..).cause_jobs`, hestia.rs:977-988) and waiting requests holding a `Gate under review: NAME.` line (hestia.rs:1079, 1140-1147) are fixes too. No key or title match, and no work-item lookup.
decisions.reason: The critic is right. `RequestQueue::apply` is the only writer of channel `steward` (steward.rs:662-683) and `decide` applies every item the steward may change as such a request (steward.rs:710-714), whatever the item's kind. So the channel already identifies the steward's requests, blind-spot, repeated-failure and Proposal-kind alike, and the website guard handles the owner's exclusion. The earlier last-job-evidence link and its `decide` order test are dropped. Hestia files its requests with `athena queue`, channel `cli` (reading.rs:976-981), so for Hestia the plan uses what the records link, as hestia.rs:957-958 requires. The steward half reuses `improvement_requests`, so the fix set and the guaranteed turn agree on which steward requests are open; an interrupted (dispatched) steward job is in neither and keeps its age place.

rejected.option: Lookup through steward work items (kind BlindSpot or RepeatedFailure, last job evidence).
rejected.why: The steward's model items other than RepeatedFailure are recorded as Proposal (steward.rs:1045-1048), so most of its requests would not be ranked; the channel is a direct, stable marker.

rejected.option: Match 'root cause' or 'gate' in a key or title, as the accepted reading allowed.
rejected.why: A person's request with a similar title would jump the queue and a reworded steward title would drop out; hestia.rs:957 says never by title.

rejected.option: Flag every steward-channel request with no guard.
rejected.why: The owner says the steward's website and study content requests are not fixes.

rejected.option: Also flag the throughput design request and the spec-review requests that `improvement_of` lists.
rejected.why: The owner names root-cause, repeated-failure, blind-spot and gate-review requests only. Those two keep their guaranteed turn; one more line in `fix_requests_of` adds them if the owner wants it.

decisions.choice: Finding 6: website and study content is `WEBSITE_PATHS = ["studies/", "xtask/src/site.rs", "xtask/src/decisions.rs", "xtask/tests/site_page.rs", "xtask/tests/fixtures/", ".github/workflows/pages.yml"]` in topics.rs. `is_website_request(text)` is true when `request_text_touches(text)` is non-empty and every path starts with one of them. Any other path (`crates/`, `records/`, `docs/`, `xtask/src/shard.rs`) makes the request a fix.
decisions.reason: Every sentence of the page comes from `studies/firstmate-work-handling` (xtask/src/site.rs:3-5). The page and decisions page are rendered by `site.rs` and `decisions.rs` (site.rs:18-19), and past website work edits those files with `intro.json` (HISTORY.txt lines 335-338, 425-428, 1076-1079). The rest of `xtask/` (`ci_cache.rs`, `shard.rs`, `walltime.rs`, `main.rs`) is Athena's own build and CI tooling, so it stays a fix. Page text hard-coded in `site.rs` cannot be told from generator logic by path, so a request that edits only `site.rs` is treated as website work; D181 says so. A website request that also names a non-website path counts as a fix. `StewardRequest::new` always writes a `Files:` line of at least one path (steward.rs:568-570), so a steward request always has paths to read. The guard reads the request's own text, which never changes, so the flag is the same before and after a read (topics.rs:397-413 replaces `touches` with the reading's deliverables). A unit test checks that every listed path exists in the repository so a rename cannot silently shrink the set.

rejected.why: It lives in the cli crate, and it would demote steward fixes to Athena's CI tooling under `xtask/`.
Website requests that edit `site.rs` or `decisions.rs` would be ranked as fixes, against the owner's exclusion.
It flips to the reading's deliverables after a read, so the same item would rank differently before and after.

decisions.choice: Compute the fix set once per `queue()` and once per `plan_entry()` with `hestia::fix_requests_of`, pass it to `entry_of`, and set `entry.fix = fixes.contains(job)` there. `reading::plan_entry` stays free of records and leaves `fix` false.
decisions.reason: `entry_of` runs once per queued item (drain.rs:4527-4530) and the Hestia link scans introspections, so one set per call keeps the cost flat with 50 or more steward requests; `improvement()` already does the same scan on every re-plan (drain.rs:4568-4572). `plan_entry` also builds the entry that replaces the queue entry after a read (drain.rs:2282), so it must set the flag too. One function owns the rule, so there is one definition of 'fix'. The only production caller of `reading::plan_entry` is drain.rs:4364.

rejected.option: Set the steward half inside `reading::plan_entry` from the job's channel.
rejected.why: It splits one rule over two places; the Hestia half needs the records.

rejected.option: Compute the flag inside `entry_of` for each job.
rejected.why: It repeats the records scan for every queued item.

decisions.choice: Cap slots follow the plan order, so inside a full tier a fix request keeps its slot ahead of an older feature request. Person-set priorities are still counted first and never demoted. The consequence is stated in D181, in the CHANGELOG entry and in the `athena drain --help` text (finding 7), and tested.
decisions.reason: `build_capped` hands out slots in the uncapped plan order (plan.rs:811-818, 847-865); its doc says the others keep slots 'in the plan's own order' (plan.rs:801-802). The fix flag is now part of that order. Making slots ignore it needs a second uncapped build, which is a rule of its own. Hestia's root-cause requests are queued High (hestia.rs:1012-1014), so a non-person high feature request can be demoted to normal in favour of one; the cap values do not change, only which item holds a slot. The same text says that a person's `athena priority <job> <level>` record still wins over the flag.

rejected.option: Compute the slots from an order with the flag cleared.
rejected.why: A second build and a second ordering rule for a case the owner did not ask about.

decisions.choice: Findings 1 to 4: keep four files outside the listed deliverables, each for a stated reason: hestia.rs (the `fix_requests_of` function), main.rs (the `athena drain --help` Order text), README.md (one sentence) and docs/design/roles-and-ladder.md (one sentence). None is a governance file.
decisions.reason: hestia.rs: `GATE_LINE` is private (hestia.rs:1079) and hestia.rs:957-958 owns the rule that requests are found by what the records link; a copy of the literal in a listed file would give one marker two definitions. If the host refuses the file, the fallback is to drop the gate-review half and put the steward half and `improvement_of(..).cause_jobs` in drain.rs (both public), and D181 would say so. main.rs: the help is what the owner reads, and critic finding 7 asks for the cap-slot consequence there; D156 (decisions.md:4271-4273) records a job rejected because its change left that help false. README.md:148 ('age only breaks ties') and roles-and-ladder.md:73-74 ('ordered by rung (top first), then age') would become false. grep found no test that pins those words. Each edit is one sentence. docs/ontology.toml:31 ('by rung and age') already omits priority and dependencies; it stays a coarse summary and D181 names it.

rejected.option: Change only the listed deliverables and name the other texts as stale.
rejected.why: A known-false sentence in the help and the README is the failure D156 describes.

rejected.option: Match the gate literal in topics.rs or drain.rs.
rejected.why: It duplicates a private marker with nothing tying the copy to the original.

decisions.choice: The accepted reading's 'approved work item' route is not built. A work item the steward applies is a queued request on the steward channel; an approved item is always a Proposal and its job is a person-channel job.
decisions.reason: `find_open` refuses any kind other than Proposal (work_decisions.rs:107-109) and `open_proposals` lists only Proposals (work_decisions.rs:51-63), so an approved item is never a BlindSpot or RepeatedFailure. `approve_work` submits the job through `ask` (work_decisions.rs:344-345), channel `cli` (reading.rs:955). Items the steward applies directly are covered by the channel rule. An approved owner-bound proposal keeps its place by rung and age; D181 states it.

rejected.option: Flag jobs that carry out an approved steward proposal.
rejected.why: They are owner-bound environment or token requests, not the fixes the owner lists, and the owner did not name them.

risks.risk: Every open steward request that is not website content now ranks ahead of same-priority person requests, so normal feature work can wait behind a long run of steward requests. This is the goal the owner set, but it moves the starvation to the other side.
risks.mitigation: A person's `athena priority <job> <level>` record or urgent/high words still decide before the flag, and the guaranteed turn is unchanged. The help text, D181 and the CHANGELOG say plainly that feature work of the same tier waits for ready steward fix requests.

risks.risk: How many of the 52 requests the rule ranks is not known: the records are absent from the snapshot, and the website guard removes the ones whose own text names only website paths.
risks.mitigation: D181 and the CHANGELOG say the share was not measured. The tests show the guard on each side of the line.

risks.risk: Website paths are a hard-coded list; a renamed file silently drops out, and page text hard-coded in `xtask/src/site.rs` cannot be told from generator logic by path.
risks.mitigation: A unit test checks that every listed path exists. D181 states that a request editing only `site.rs` or `decisions.rs` counts as website work, and a request naming any other path counts as a fix.

risks.risk: A non-person high feature request can lose a cap slot to a high fix request (Hestia's root-cause requests are queued High, hestia.rs:1012-1014) and be demoted to normal sooner than before. This sits near the out-of-scope 'caps' item.
risks.mitigation: The cap values and demotion rules are unchanged; person-set items are counted first and never demoted. The consequence is chosen, tested, and written in the help text, the CHANGELOG entry and D181 so the owner sees it.

risks.risk: A person's request that cites a repeated cause's introspection ids or holds a `Gate under review:` line also counts as a fix, because hestia.rs:967-968 links by what a request cites, not who wrote it.
risks.mitigation: This matches the existing guaranteed-turn rule, so the two stay consistent. D181 states it.

risks.risk: Four files outside the listed deliverables change (hestia.rs, main.rs, README.md, roles-and-ladder.md), which widens the scope.
risks.mitigation: Each change is small, has a stated reason in decision 6 and is not a governance file. If the host refuses hestia.rs, the fallback is to compute the steward half and the root-cause half in drain.rs from the public `steward::improvement_requests` and `improvement_of(..).cause_jobs`, drop the gate-review half, and say so in D181.

risks.risk: The fix set scans the records once per `queue()` and `plan_entry()`, and `fix_requests_of` runs `improvement_of`, which scans introspections.
risks.mitigation: It runs once per call, not once per item, and `RealSteps::improvement` already runs the same scan on every re-plan (drain.rs:4568-4572).

risks.risk: The criterion 3 and 4 fixtures could leave a request without a rung, which would refuse it, or give the requests different rungs so age no longer decides.
risks.mitigation: Each steward request is built through `StewardRequest`, which always writes an acceptance bullet and a `Files:` line (steward.rs:535-595), and each names a path, so `infer_rung` gives Implementation without a read (topics.rs:256-259). The tests assert equal rungs and that every item is in `plan.order` before they assert the order.

risks.risk: The new CHANGELOG, D181 and README text could trip the boundary-word scan or name a person.
risks.mitigation: The text calls the requester 'the owner' and names no person, machine or email; `cargo test --locked` runs the policy scan.

demonstrations.method: Unit test `a_ready_fix_entry_comes_before_an_older_feature_entry_of_the_same_tier` in the `mod tests` of crates/athena-core/src/plan.rs. Entries come from the existing `entry(id, rung, touches, deps)` helper (plan.rs:1159): an older normal entry `feature` first in the slice, then a newer normal entry `fix` with `fix = true`. It calls `Plan::build_with`, and `Plan::build_improving` with `TierCaps::UNLIMITED`, an empty `person_set` and `Improvement::default()` (the call `athena plan` and `athena drain` make, drain.rs:2367). It also runs the same two entries with `fix` false as a control, and a case where the fix entry has the lower rung (Implementation against BriefRequirements), so rung order cannot be what put it first.
demonstrations.observes: `plan.order == ["fix", "feature"]` from both builders, including with the fix entry on the lower rung. The control with `fix` false gives `["feature", "fix"]`.
demonstrations.fails_without: With the sort key left at `(e.rung, *age)` the newer fix entry stays behind the older feature entry, so the `plan.order` assertion fails and the control would not differ from the flagged run.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry points `Plan::build_with` (plan.rs:692) and `Plan::build_improving` (plan.rs:894) exist. The fixture is plain `PlanEntry` data from the existing `entry` helper; nothing is doubled. The `fix` field and the new key are added by plan steps 1 and 2.

demonstrations.method: Two unit tests in plan.rs `mod tests`. (1) `the_fix_flag_never_overrides_priority_or_dependencies`, through `Plan::build_with` with `with_priority` (plan.rs:1662): (a) an older urgent feature, an older high feature and a newer normal fix; (b) a normal fix that depends on a newer normal non-fix with a lower rung; (c) a normal non-fix that is a dependency of a high feature, beside a normal fix; (d) two fix and two feature entries in one tier with different rungs and ages. (2) `the_fix_flag_decides_a_full_tier_slot_in_plan_order`, through `Plan::build_capped` with `TierCaps { urgent: 3, high: 1 }`: an older high feature `f` and a newer high fix `x`, first with an empty `person_set`, then with `person_set = ["f"]`.
demonstrations.observes: (a) order urgent, high, fix. (b) the prerequisite comes before the fix entry that needs it. (c) the prerequisite is raised to high by `effective_priorities` (plan.rs:758) and comes before the normal fix. (d) both fix entries, then both feature entries, each pair by rung then age. Test two with an empty person set: `plan.order == ["x", "f"]`, `plan.demoted` holds one entry for `f` (High to Normal, cap 1) and the capped copy of `x` is still High. With `f` in `person_set`: `f` keeps the slot, `x` is demoted and the order is `["f", "x"]`.
demonstrations.fails_without: A key that put the flag above effective priority, or sorted before the best-tier filter, puts the normal fix ahead of the urgent and high features in (a) and ahead of the raised prerequisite in (c). A key that ignored `depends_on` puts the dependent fix first in (b). Without the flag in the order, test two's `x` would not take the slot and `f` would not be demoted. Each fails an order or demotion assertion.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry points `Plan::build_with` (plan.rs:692) and `Plan::build_capped` (plan.rs:804) exist. Fixtures are `PlanEntry` values with `priority`, `depends_on` and `fix` set through the existing `entry` and `with_priority` helpers. The `fix` field is added by plan step 1. Nothing is doubled.

demonstrations.method: Integration test `a_steward_website_or_study_content_request_is_not_a_fix_and_keeps_its_age_place` in crates/athena-cli/tests/drain.rs on the real `Fixture`, `fx.athena(Scenario::default().script())` and `real_steps` (the pattern of `drain_order_equals_plan_order`, tests/drain.rs:6394). It queues an older person feature request with `athena.queue(&complete_request("crates/f/lib.rs", ""))` (tests/drain.rs:6319). It then queues four steward-channel requests with `queue_steward_request` (tests/drain.rs:2573, which goes through `RequestQueue::apply` as the steward does): website content naming only `studies/demo/intro.json`, site generator naming only `xtask/src/site.rs`, and CI tooling naming only `xtask/src/shard.rs`, in that order. It calls `drain::plan(&Replay::new(real_steps(..), None), 5.0, &Quiet)` and reads `PlanReport::entries` and `plan.order`. It also calls `RealSteps::plan_entry(job)` for the content and the tooling request, the path the read pass takes. Supporting core tests: `cargo test -p athena-core website_request` (topics.rs `is_website_request` table: studies only true; studies plus `crates/` false; no path false; `xtask/src/site.rs` only true; `xtask/src/shard.rs` false; pages.yml true; ci.yml false; `studies-extra/x.json` false; every listed path exists) and `cargo test -p athena-core fix_requests_of` (the hestia.rs test, see criterion 4 plan step 3).
demonstrations.observes: All entries have rung Some(Implementation), checked first, so age and not rung decides, and none is in `refused`. `plan.order == [shard_request, feature, studies_request, site_request]`. The two website entries have `fix == false`, the CI tooling entry has `fix == true`, and `RealSteps::plan_entry` returns the same flags.
demonstrations.fails_without: If the classifier flagged every steward-channel request, both website requests would move ahead of the older feature request and the order and `fix == false` assertions fail. If it flagged nothing, the tooling request would stay last and the order assertion fails. If the flag were set only in `queue()` and not in `plan_entry()`, the `plan_entry` assertion fails.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry points `drain::plan` (drain.rs:3448), `RealSteps::queue` (drain.rs:4483) and `RealSteps::plan_entry` (drain.rs:4543) exist, as do `Fixture`, `queue_steward_request`, `complete_request`, `Replay` and `real_steps`. Records are real and committed to the fixture repository. Plan steps 3 to 5 add `is_website_request`, `fix_requests_of` and the wiring in `queue()` and `plan_entry()`. Only the scripted agent and `RecordingLander` stand in, and neither orders anything.

demonstrations.method: Integration tests in crates/athena-cli/tests/drain.rs. Test A, `a_steward_request_is_dispatched_before_an_older_feature_request_of_the_same_priority`: queue an older person feature request with `athena.queue(&complete_request("crates/f/lib.rs", ""))`; then a newer person request with the steward's text (`crates/s/lib.rs`), which is the control; then the newest, the steward's applied blind-spot item through the new helper `steward_applies` (plan step 7). The helper calls the real `steward::decide` with `athena_data::roles::steward(ts)` and `RequestQueue` and commits the queued request file and the `WorkItem` (kind BlindSpot, key `blind-spot:jobs`, evidence citing the queued job), exactly as the steward writes them (steward.rs:698-741), with no decision record. Run `drain::plan` and then `drain::drain(&Replay::new(real_steps(..), None), limits(100.0), &Quiet)`, and read `Replay::started`. Test B, `a_steward_request_is_dispatched_before_an_older_feature_request_whatever_the_item_kind`: for each kind BlindSpot, RepeatedFailure and Proposal, a fresh fixture with an older person feature request and the steward's applied item for that kind; `drain::plan` only.
demonstrations.observes: Test A: all three entries have rung Some(Implementation) and are in `plan.order`, none refused. `plan.order == [steward, feature, control]`: the person-channel copy of the same text keeps its age place behind the older feature request, the steward request goes first. The steward entry has `fix == true`, the other two `false`. After `drain::drain`, `started == plan.order` and `started[0]` is the steward job. Test B: `plan.order[0]` is the steward job for all three kinds.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without `fix_requests_of` in `queue()` or without the new sort key, the older feature request is dispatched first and `started[0]` is the feature job. If the flag keyed on the person channel or on text alone, the control copy would also move first and the order assertion fails. If the classifier needed a work item of kind BlindSpot or RepeatedFailure, the Proposal case of test B fails.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry points `drain::plan`, `drain::drain` (drain.rs:3008) and `RealSteps` exist, as do `Fixture`, `Replay` (`started`), `real_steps`, `limits`, `complete_request` and `commit_records_to`. Plan steps 1 to 5 add the field, the key, `fix_requests_of` and the wiring; step 7 adds `steward_applies`, built on the existing `Committer` use in `queue_steward_request` (tests/drain.rs:2586-2599). `decide` is production code and is not doubled. Only the scripted agent and `RecordingLander` stand in.

demonstrations.observes: A new `## D181 · ...` entry in the D180 layout with Case, Decision, Alternatives, Tradeoff, Reversal cost and Provenance bullets. The Case cites the owner's request and its figure (52 steward requests filed in the week to 14 Nov that never ran), says the figure was stated and not re-measured, and says the records are absent from the snapshot. The Decision states the sort key, the channel rule, the Hestia links, the website path set with the reason `site.rs` counts as website, and the cap-slot consequence. The Tradeoff lists the limits: how many of the 52 are website requests (and so not ranked) is not measured; a website request that also names a non-website path counts as a fix; a person's request citing a repeated cause or holding the gate line also counts; throughput and spec requests and interrupted steward jobs are not ranked; normal feature work waits behind ready steward fix requests of its tier unless a person sets a higher priority; a non-person high feature request can lose a cap slot to a high fix request. It names docs/ontology.toml:31 as a coarse summary left unchanged. CHANGELOG.md gains one entry under `## [Unreleased]` / `### Added` naming job 20261114-041129-dwmx, the root cause, the rule, the cap-slot consequence, the limits and the tests. No personal name and no email appear.
